---
title: "Racial Concentration in Sarasota County, Florida"
execute:
  echo: false
  message: false
  warning: false
---

Sarasota County, Florida, presents a striking example of geographic racial segregation. According to the 2020 Decennial Census, the median census tract in Sarasota County has a Black or African American population of just 1.2%. However, in North Sarasota, **Census Tract 3**—which encompasses the historic African American community of Newtown—is **74.5% Black**.

```{r}
#| label: map-sarasota-race
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

# Load pre-downloaded Census tract data and compute percentages
sarasota <- read_rds("sarasota_race.rds") |>
  mutate(
    pct_black = if_else(total > 0, 100 * (black / total), NA_real_)
  )

# Map Black population share by census tract
ggplot(sarasota) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_black), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    direction = -1,
    name = "% Black",
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "Black Population Share by Census Tract",
    subtitle = "Sarasota County, FL (2020 Decennial Census)",
    caption = "Source: US Census Bureau (Table P2)"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray30", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

### The History of Newtown

Newtown was established in 1914 when Black residents were pushed out of downtown Sarasota's Overtown neighborhood during Jim Crow segregation. Over a century later, the Census data shows how strongly historical settlement patterns persist in Sarasota's neighborhood demographics today.
